findings.description: The inline policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:* and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", giving the deploy user full control of every EC2, S3, Lambda and CloudWatch resource in the account. This violates least privilege: the identity can read/modify/delete all stored data (s3:*), manipulate compute (ec2:*, lambda:*), and tamper with logging (cloudwatch:*) across the whole account, and lambda:* combined with ec2:* provides privilege-escalation paths (e.g. creating a function with an existing privileged role).

This output emits IAM access key material. Outputs are not marked sensitive and are written to Terraform state and displayed in plan/apply logs and CI output, so the credential is exposed to anyone with state or log access. The key is not tied to a pgp_key, so secret material associated with this key is stored unprotected in state.

A static, long-lived IAM access key is created for the deploy user. Because it is attached to the broadly privileged svc_deploy_policy, compromise of this single key yields account-wide control of EC2, S3, Lambda and CloudWatch. Static keys have no expiry or rotation and persist in Terraform state, unlike short-lived role credentials.
